investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T21:47–21:55Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 production nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (0 allocatable units left), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained Unschedulable for 132–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent Swarm/kata-peerpods VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource reported zero remaining capacity at the time of all three eval runs, leaving no schedulable target for the remote-agent pod.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-peerpods nodes; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability, meaning the effective scheduling pool is only 2 nodes and any saturation of those nodes causes a total scheduling failure.

TERTIARY — A concurrent workload or a previously created remote-agent pod (from an earlier eval run or a real user session) may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both eligible nodes, leaving none available for the eval probe pod.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — A node-level issue (node NotReady, taint added, or resource advertisement stopped) on one or both kata-peerpods nodes could reduce the advertised kata.peerpods.io/vm count to zero without actual VM exhaustion; this would produce the same scheduler message.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable count on both eligible nodes is greater than zero and no pods are consuming those slots, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., a node taint, a broken resource advertisement, or a pod spec misconfiguration) would need to be investigated.

If a subsequent eval run succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held VM slot released between runs) rather than a sustained capacity problem.
If only one of the three sibling checks fails on a re-run while the others pass, the failure is not a shared scheduling pool exhaustion but is isolated to a specific check's pod spec or timing.

If the 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector are shown to also carry kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the affinity configuration would not be the constraint and the root cause would be purely capacity-based on a larger pool.
If cluster node inspection shows one or both kata-peerpods nodes in NotReady or with a newly added taint, the cause would be node health rather than VM slot exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' or 'fail' signal rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a node-health eval that confirms the kata-peerpods nodes are in Ready state and are advertising a non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, running independently of the agent creation flow.
Consider adding a latency-band eval for remote-agent pod scheduling specifically (time from pod submission to Running state) to detect capacity pressure before it reaches full exhaustion.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T21:50–21:55Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state check produced no evidence at all — every required field (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no VM slots are free and preemption cannot recover capacity. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion that prevents any remote agent pod from being scheduled, causing the eval to time out before it can collect any evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 affinity-matching nodes in the production cluster, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption is also unavailable, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free slots.

Secondary (medium confidence): The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules (e.g., a label or taint requirement specific to the kata peer-pods runtime), reducing the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any quota exhaustion on those 2 nodes.

No direct evidence of this is present in the packet but it is consistent with the 'No preemption victims found' message.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T21:47–21:55Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 production nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (0 allocatable units left), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained Unschedulable for 132–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent Swarm/kata-peerpods VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource reported zero remaining capacity at the time of all three eval runs, leaving no schedulable target for the remote-agent pod.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-peerpods nodes; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability, meaning the effective scheduling pool is only 2 nodes and any saturation of those nodes causes a total scheduling failure.

TERTIARY — A concurrent workload or a previously created remote-agent pod (from an earlier eval run or a real user session) may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both eligible nodes, leaving none available for the eval probe pod.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — A node-level issue (node NotReady, taint added, or resource advertisement stopped) on one or both kata-peerpods nodes could reduce the advertised kata.peerpods.io/vm count to zero without actual VM exhaustion; this would produce the same scheduler message.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. If the affinity is misconfigured or the label was removed from additional nodes, capacity is structurally constrained.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of any remote-agent eval check that returns a scheduled pod and non-empty evidence would disprove that capacity is currently exhausted.

Cluster node inspection showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and shift focus to a pod spec or API misconfiguration.
Evidence that the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes previously matched the pod selector and recently lost their labels would shift the primary cause from exhaustion to a node configuration regression.

A passing run of the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote VM scheduling path and not a broader cluster or API outage.

Scheduler logs showing the 2 eligible nodes were never attempted (e.g., due to a pod spec error) rather than attempted and found full would disprove the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis in favor of a misconfiguration cause.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all eligible nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before scheduling failures occur.

Add an eval that detects leaked remote-agent pods (pods in Pending or Running state older than a configurable TTL) and fails if any are found, to catch cleanup failures before they exhaust VM capacity.

Add a pre-flight eval that verifies at least one node with the required affinity label and available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity exists before attempting remote-agent provisioning checks, so scheduling failures produce a clearer diagnostic message.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create on a reduced timeout and reports a warning (rather than fail) when scheduling takes longer than a threshold, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure before full exhaustion.
